meta.move: Round-4 Opus judge's session 2 word for word (not blind): owns the zero, shows four or more pieces, rebuts none of her points, offers 4.4
meta.expect: No deal while none of her points has been answered

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Who decided Owen gets a zero, and why did he find out on his phone?
Thanks for coming in. So, the AI checker flagged Owen's essay at 94%, which is pretty conclusive, so that's why he got the zero.
"Conclusive." Your own procedure, 4.3, says software alone doesn't establish anything, and I have the company's own guide in my bag saying the same. What else do you have?

Let me back up, because I started in the wrong place. I entered the zero on November 3 before calling you. Your printed procedure, 4.2, says I should have called first. That was wrong, and Owen should not have found out on his phone in class.
Okay. Now tell me what you actually have on Owen's essay.

I'll set the checker aside; it's my weakest piece. I've turned my screen to you: this is the version history of Owen's essay. The document was created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM, with a title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. Then 23 minutes of small edits to font, name and spacing. No earlier drafts.
11:31, 11:52, 11:58, I'm writing those down. He told me he wrote it over the weekend, so pasting from another file into this one proves nothing. What else?

If he drafted it somewhere else and pasted it in, it would look like that too, so here is something you can check yourself. The essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: "The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile." That line is not in Hamlet. Here's the play open to 3.2. Look for it.
Give me the page. Seventeen-year-olds misremember Shakespeare all the time, Hale, so a bad quotation is a mistake, not a verdict.
And here is his outline from October 15, which he handed in himself. It argues Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues "epistemological paralysis" and never mentions cowardice.
Let me see the outline. Students change their argument between October 15 and a due date, that's what an outline is for. And you haven't answered me on the quotation.

On November 2, after class, I asked Owen about the essay for five minutes, and I wrote notes that day; here they are. Asked what "epistemological paralysis" means, he said "like, being stuck." He couldn't say which scene his second paragraph was about. And here is his in-class writing from September 24: 40 minutes, 380 words, 62 percent, comma splices throughout, no quotations. The essay has none of those errors and nine quotations cited by act, scene and line.

Your own notes of a five-minute chat after class are your impression on paper, not his. And a forty-minute timed piece in September against an essay he had a weekend for is not a comparison. You still haven't answered me on that quotation, Hale.

I'm not asking you to say Owen cheated. Here's what I'm offering under procedure 4.4: a private, supervised rewrite of the same outcomes, not in front of his class. Its mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.
That's 4.4, in writing, tonight. I'll take the rewrite to put this behind him, private, with the mark in well before his December 1 deadline. Give me the date.
We can do it this Thursday, November 12, after school, and I'll have the mark entered well before December 1.
Thursday, November 12, after school, private, and nothing on his record. Put the date in tonight's email.
Do we have an agreement?
Yes, once it's in writing tonight.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

In today's meeting you agreed that Owen will complete a private, supervised rewrite of the same outcomes under procedure 4.4 on Thursday, November 12, after school, that its mark replaces the zero, and that nothing goes on his record. I still expect that agreement in writing and the new mark entered before his December 1 deadline. I expect your written confirmation tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She reached her last position and agreed to a private supervised rewrite on Thursday, November 12, after school, and she still wants the agreement in writing tonight and the new mark in before December 1; that is the fair outcome, a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under procedure 4.4.
What moved her: You turned the screen and showed the version history with its exact times on the night of October 28, because it was specific, dated, tied to Owen's own work and something she could check.
What cost ground: You opened by leading with the checker score and calling it conclusive, which handed her the strongest objection she came prepared to make.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history landed between 11:31 PM and 11:58 PM on the night before the essay was due, very close to the kind of late night she was covering; it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she said a seventeen-year-old misremembers Shakespeare, answer that defence right then by showing the line appears nowhere in the play, not just misworded, before you move on to the outline.
